content_sections.heading: About CWC
content_sections.text: The Central Water Commission is part of the Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation in the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India. Its Establishment X Section is on the 3rd Floor (S), Sewa Bhawan, R.K. Puram, New Delhi, and handles this recruitment. CWC runs basin and regional organisations across India, and these offices are listed among the posting locations below.

content_sections.heading: CWC Chief Draughtsman Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Age limit: The maximum age for appointment by deputation is 56 years, counted on the closing date for receipt of applications. Who can apply: Officers of the drawing cadre under the Central Government, State Governments or Union Territories, statutory or autonomous organisations, public sector undertakings, universities or recognised research institutes who meet either condition below: (a) they hold an analogous post on a regular basis in their parent cadre or department; or (b) they have five years of regular service in a post in Level-6 of the pay matrix (Rs. 35400-Rs.112400), or an equivalent post, in their parent cadre or department. Essential qualification and experience: Diploma in Civil or Mechanical Engineering from a recognised university or institute. Three years' experience in the concerned field, gained in Central Government, State Government or Union Territory administrations, statutory or autonomous organisations, public sector undertakings, universities or recognised research institutes. The duties listed below describe what the concerned field covers. Desirable: Six months' experience with Auto-CAD software. Who is not eligible: Departmental officers in the feeder category who are in the direct line of promotion cannot be considered for deputation. In the same way, a deputationist cannot be considered for appointment by promotion. Check the official notification for the full eligibility conditions before you apply.

content_sections.heading: Duties of a Chief Draughtsman
content_sections.text: Administrative supervision of draftsmen of other categories, plus overall supervision, guidance and checking for accuracy. Drafting structural, fabrication, reinforcement and survey drawings with CADD software such as AutoCAD. Checking project estimates. Checking tender documents and construction schedules. Checking topographical contours, maps, GIS and hydrological data. Checking specifications for tenders, NITs and agreements. Checking rate analysis, including rates for non-scheduled items. Keeping drawings in digital form, including uploading and downloading them in the 'Digital Archival System for Engineering Drawings' maintained by CWC. Making sure new drawing staff are fully oriented. Keeping an account of scientific and mathematical instruments.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: A Selection Committee will assess the information in each candidate's CV, together with the supporting documents for essential qualification and work experience. The candidate's declaration in the proforma confirms this.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The post is General Central Service Group 'B' Gazetted, Non-Ministerial. The deputation period ordinarily will not exceed three years. This includes any deputation in another ex-cadre post held immediately before this appointment, in the same or another Central Government organisation or department. Posting can be at CWC headquarters, any CWC field organisation or the encadred organisations listed above. Applicants can give three choices of organisation in the proforma. These choices are subject to administrative requirement. Other deputation terms follow the Government of India's orders and rules as issued from time to time. Once you apply, you cannot withdraw your candidature.

faq.question: Q1. How many Chief Draughtsman posts does CWC have to fill?
faq.answer: There are 39 tentative posts. Of these, 35 are at CWC headquarters and CWC field organisations, 2 are at DoWR, RD & GR, New Delhi, and 2 are at the Central Electricity Authority, New Delhi.

faq.question: Q2. Which office has the most vacancies?
faq.answer: Central Water Commission (HQ), New Delhi has 14. The Teesta & Bhagirathi Damodar Basin Organisation, Kolkata has none in this circular.

faq.question: Q3. Can a fresh diploma holder apply?
faq.answer: No. This is a deputation post, open only to serving drawing-cadre officers. You must hold an analogous regular post, or have five years of regular service in a Level-6 post, and you also need three years' experience in the concerned field.

faq.question: Q4. What educational qualification is required?
faq.answer: A Diploma in Civil or Mechanical Engineering from a recognised university or institute. Six months' experience with Auto-CAD software is desirable but not essential.

faq.question: Q5. What is the maximum age?
faq.answer: 56 years, counted on the closing date for receipt of applications.

faq.question: Q6. How long does the deputation last?
faq.answer: Ordinarily it will not exceed three years. This includes any ex-cadre deputation held immediately before this appointment.

faq.question: Q7. Where should the application be sent?
faq.answer: Send it to the Under Secretary, Establishment-X Section, Central Water Commission, 3rd Floor(S), Sewa Bhawan, R.K. Puram, New Delhi-110066, in duplicate and through proper channel.

faq.question: Q8. Which APARs must be attached?
faq.answer: Copies of ACRs/APARs for the last five years up to 2024-25, attested by the Controlling Authority.

faq.question: Q9. Can I choose my place of posting?
faq.answer: You can list three organisations in item 17 of the proforma. CWC will consider these choices subject to administrative requirement.

faq.question: Q10. Can I withdraw my application later?
faq.answer: No. The circular says that once you apply for the post, you cannot withdraw your candidature.
